topics.title: Limits
topics.description: The foundation of calculus — understanding what a function approaches as input approaches a value.
objectives: Define the limit of a function informally and formally (epsilon-delta)
Evaluate limits algebraically and graphically
Apply limit laws to compute limits
Identify and classify discontinuities

problem_templates.prompt_template: Evaluate the limit algebraically: lim_{x→2} (x²−4)/(x−2). Show each factoring step and explain why direct substitution fails.
Determine whether lim_{x→0} sin(x)/x exists. Evaluate it using the squeeze theorem and explain each bound.
Use the epsilon-delta definition to prove that lim_{x→3} (2x−1) = 5. Explicitly construct δ in terms of ε.

topics.title: Derivatives
topics.description: The instantaneous rate of change of a function — defined as the limit of the difference quotient.
objectives: Define the derivative as a limit
Interpret the derivative as slope of tangent line and rate of change
Compute derivatives from the definition
Understand differentiability vs. continuity

problem_templates.prompt_template: Using the limit definition of the derivative, find f'(x) for f(x) = x² + 3x. Write out every step of the difference quotient.
Find the equation of the tangent line to f(x) = √x at x = 4. Use the derivative to find the slope; show your work.
Show that f(x) = |x| is continuous but not differentiable at x = 0. Prove both claims rigorously using limits.

topics.title: Differentiation Rules
topics.description: Systematic rules for computing derivatives: power, product, quotient, and chain rules.
objectives: Apply power, constant, and sum/difference rules
Use the product and quotient rules
Apply the chain rule to composite functions
Differentiate trigonometric, exponential, and logarithmic functions

problem_templates.prompt_template: Differentiate h(x) = (x³ + 2x)(sin x). Apply the product rule step-by-step and simplify.
Find dy/dx for y = e^(x²·ln x). Apply the chain rule and product rule, identifying each composite layer.
Differentiate f(x) = (sin(x²))/(1 + cos x) and find all critical points on [0, 2π]. Show the quotient and chain rule applications.

topics.title: Integration
topics.description: The antiderivative and the definite integral as the area under a curve.
objectives: Define the indefinite integral as antiderivative
Compute definite integrals using Riemann sums
Apply basic integration rules
Understand the relationship between integration and area

problem_templates.prompt_template: Compute ∫(3x² − 5x + 2) dx. Apply the power rule for integration term-by-term and include the constant of integration.
Evaluate ∫₀¹ x·e^(x²) dx using substitution. Identify u, compute du, transform the bounds, and evaluate.
Approximate ∫₁³ (1/x) dx using a right Riemann sum with n=4 subintervals, then compare to the exact value. Compute the absolute error.

topics.title: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
topics.description: Connects differentiation and integration, showing they are inverse operations.
objectives: State and prove both parts of the Fundamental Theorem
Use FTC Part 1 to differentiate integral functions
Use FTC Part 2 to evaluate definite integrals
Apply the theorem to solve applied problems

problem_templates.prompt_template: Use FTC Part 2 to evaluate ∫₀^π sin(x) dx. State the antiderivative, apply the evaluation theorem, and give the exact value.
Find d/dx[∫₁^(x²) √(1+t³) dt] using FTC Part 1 combined with the chain rule. Show each step.
A particle moves with velocity v(t) = t² − 4t + 3. Use the FTC to find the displacement and total distance travelled on [0, 4]. Distinguish between the two.

topics.title: Series and Sequences
topics.description: Infinite sequences, convergence, and series including Taylor and power series.
objectives: Define convergence and divergence of sequences
Apply convergence tests for series
Construct Taylor and Maclaurin series
Determine radius and interval of convergence

problem_templates.prompt_template: Determine whether the series Σ(1/n²) from n=1 to ∞ converges or diverges. Apply the p-series test and state its conditions.
Derive the Maclaurin series for f(x) = cos(x) up to the x⁶ term. Show the pattern of derivatives at x=0 and identify the general term.
Find the radius and interval of convergence for the power series Σ (n·xⁿ)/(3ⁿ) from n=0 to ∞. Apply the ratio test and check endpoints.
